title: Many Buddhas, many worlds
hookLine: countless Buddhas in countless worlds, each with a land
last: THREE BODIES: TRUTH, GLORY, AND A LIFE ON REAL ROADS.

lines: AS MANY AS THE SANDS OF THE GANGES.
cards: How big is the universe in a Buddhist sutra? In the short sutra on the land of bliss, the Buddha turns to his disciple Shariputra and starts naming Buddhas. Buddhas in the east, each with a world of their own.
Then the south, the west, the north, the regions below and above. After each list comes the same refrain: and more besides, as many as the grains of sand in the river Ganges.
Our world, in this picture, is one small place among a great many.

teach.b: First, the scale. The Pali texts already speak of world systems beyond this one. The Mahayana sutras open the view wider: space full of worlds past counting, and in many of them a Buddha teaching right now.
Each Buddha has a field, a buddhakshetra, a land shaped by that Buddha's vows and long practice. Second, one land.

teach.h: THE LAND OF BLISS IN THE WEST.
teach.b: Far to the west, the sutras say, is the land of the Buddha Amitabha: Sukhavati, the land of bliss. Jeweled trees, lotus ponds, birds whose songs are the teaching.

Long ago, as a bodhisattva, Amitabha vowed that those who turned to him with trust and called on him would be born there, where awakening comes easily. Whole schools in East Asia grew up around that vow. Third, a twist.
In the Vimalakirti Sutra, a disciple wonders privately: if a Buddha's land is pure, why does our world look so rough? The Buddha knows his thought.
He touches the ground with his toe, and for a moment everyone sees this same world shining with jewels. Then he lets it return. What you see, he says, depends on the mind that's seeing.

teach.h: WHEN THE MIND IS PURE, THE LAND IS PURE.
teach.b: When the mind is pure, the land is pure. So some Buddhists hope to be born in a pure land after this life. Others hear the pure land as this world, seen clearly.
Some hold both at once. Either way, it changes the night sky: any point of light up there might be a place where someone is teaching kindness right now.

how: Pure Land Buddhists in East Asia call on the name of Amitabha, hoping for birth in his land, and Mahayana chants and dedications often address the Buddhas of all directions.

games.q: you're a disciple, and a thought nags at you: if the Buddha's land is pure, why does this world look so rough? the Buddha knows what you're thinking. what does he do?
o: touch the ground with his toe, and the world shines
take you away to a better world
games.why: everyone sees this same world adorned with jewels. the land is like this, he says; what you see depends on the mind.

practice: If you can get to a window, look up at the widest stretch of sky you can find, or close your eyes and remember a night sky you once saw. Let the size of it be big and yourself small inside it, without that being a problem.
As you breathe, hold one thought lightly: in this old picture, somewhere out there, someone is teaching kindness right now.

wordCard.voice: Many Buddhas. The Mahayana picture of countless Buddhas in countless worlds, each in a land shaped by their vows. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: a Buddha-field, the world or land where a Buddha teaches.

carryVoice: Your line: countless worlds. Ours is just one small place among a great many. Until tomorrow.
